correctness.rationale: The published convex-curve halving-pair identity reduces dilation to the minimum halving chord. Every halving pair of a normalized isosceles trapezoid lies in one of three side-pair regimes, each with an explicit quadratic squared distance. Their constrained minima yield the exact three-branch formula for \(h\). After normalization by half-perimeter, two branches decrease in the base-imbalance parameter and one increases. The fixed-leg optimum therefore occurs at a unique crossing; the crossing type switches at a quintic with exactly one root for \(S>1\), and the two resulting optimum branches are monotone toward that junction. This proves the unique global extremum.
risks: The numerical boundary sweep is supplementary only; correctness rests on the exact branch derivation and monotonicity proof.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly identifies tight nonsymmetric polygon dilation as an unresolved direction. Isosceles trapezoids are the simplest one-parameter-symmetry enlargement of parallelograms, and the optimum is genuinely nonsymmetric and strictly improves the centrally symmetric value \(2\). The result gives a complete natural subclass theorem, a unique equality shape, and an exact algebraic balance of all possible halving-chord mechanisms.
risks: The structural value is confined to isosceles trapezoids; extending the method to arbitrary quadrilaterals requires additional halving-chord regimes.
